Part 4. You will hear a lecturer talking to a group of biology students about recent plant studies.
First you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40. Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
Good morning everyone. In the last few weeks we looked at ways in which different types of animals use their senses.
And today I'm going to introduce the topic of plant behaviour and we'll look at the
reasons why ideas about plants have been changing in the last few years.
So up until fairly recently, plants lack of eyes or ears or noses or mouths made them
less interesting to many members of the public compared to animal species.
and even by scientists they were generally regarded as organisms which were essentially
passive. However, in the last 20 years or so, evidence has started to emerge that plants
can sense their surroundings in quite sophisticated ways. But because scientific attitudes towards
plants and their capabilities had been fixed for such a long time, this evidence has
been met with some disbelief. So, let's look at some of these recent findings
that are starting to change the way some scientists view plant life.
It all began with a Canadian study that looked at a species of plant known as the Great
Lakes Sea Rocket. This is a wild plant which grows on beaches. In appearance it's perfectly
ordinary, with little purple flowers and a long stalk, but actually the plant is far from ordinary.
Normally when the sea rocket detects other plants growing nearby it quickly grows additional roots.
This is so it can compete with these other plants for the available nutrients in the soil
by soaking up as many of them as possible. But scientists found that the sea rocket doesn't
do that when the surrounding plants are related to it. And as even animals sometimes find
this type of recognition difficult, such a finding was very unexpected. It was an ability
that was previously unheard of in any other plant. Since then it's been suggested that
The two other plants may have a similar ability. These are sagebrush and thorn apple. It's
being claimed that these plants can recognise the characteristics of their neighbours by
sensing properties of the light that is reflected from them. The reason they are able to do
this is that all plant species are slightly different to each other in this respect.
So, each plant species has what you could call its own signature.
Sagebrush and Thornapple are able to recognise these.
But scientists point out that this behaviour is very different to the way that animals
sense things.
Another type of plant which can sense things in its surroundings is the Dodder plant.
This plant is different to most other species because it doesn't have the ability to
make sugar by converting nutrients from the soil. This means that as soon as the
dodder has sprouted from a seed it needs to find another plant in order to
survive. In other words, it's a parasite. Dodders infest a variety of food
crops around the world as they wrap themselves like string around their
target plants and the effect can be devastating for farmers. It's
as well as to potatoes and different varieties of citrus.
At first, scientists were puzzled as to how the dodder knows which plants to prey on.
But now they found that the plant can identify a suitable host
by sensing the chemicals that other plants release into the soil and air.
What really surprised researchers was how extremely quickly and accurately the
the dodder identifies a possible host. They used time-lapse videos to study the mechanism
and saw from these that when the dodder is trying to check out its environment, it rotates
in a circle and then, without touching any other plants, it heads directly towards its
selected host. It could sense reliably which type of plant it would grow best on. Scientists
scientists who were working on the project reported that the dodder sprout resembled
a worm as it moved towards the other plant.
Well those are some examples of the new discoveries about plant characteristics.
So which direction is plant science likely to go in next?
Many of the phenomena related to plant behaviour that I've just described are now quite
easy to observe using up-to-date equipment.
So, gradually, scientists are accepting the fact that plants are more capable than we
used to believe.
But although such plant behaviour is often obvious to some scientists…

1.why: Khách nói "It's absolutely got to be there by Friday". Thursday chỉ là mong muốn ("Ideally… by Thursday"), không phải hạn chót.

2.why: Courier Post mất 4 ngày (tới thứ Hai) nên không kịp; khách chọn "International Express… three working days" – "Okay, I'll use that then".

3.why: Hỏi địa chỉ người gửi, Peter trả lời "14 Mountain Road" (Lakeview là khu vực, không nằm trong chỗ trống).

4.why: Tên người nhận được đánh vần: "Hillman, that's H-I double L-M-A-N".

5.why: "Apartment 228, North Building" – tên toà nhà điền vào chỗ trống ngay sau số căn hộ.

6.why: "Upper Park Avenue" – đề đã cho sẵn chữ Upper, chỉ điền Park Avenue.

7.why: "I'm sending books… there are six in total" – số lượng 6 là thông tin phụ, đáp án là books.

8.why: Hỏi còn gì nữa không, khách đáp "Yes, and some photographs".

9.why: Gói hàng nặng hơn 4 kg; nhân viên chốt giá "that's going to be $98 altogether". Bẫy: số 4 (kilo) không phải giá tiền.

10.why: "Your receipt has an ID code on it which we will need to be able to trace the package". Không cần mang biên lai hay phiếu gửi, chỉ cần gọi báo ID code.

11.why: Boundary Walk hợp với người "love the coastline", khám phá đá "behind the beach" → seashore (D).

12.why: Loop Track ngắn nhưng dốc; phần thưởng là "see right down the length of the island and even across to the mainland" → views (G).

13.why: Giữa đường Puriri Walk có "a table and chairs… a great place to eat your packed lunch" → picnic area (A). Đường mòn cổ nhưng không nhắc tới toà nhà lịch sử.

14.why: North Head đi qua rừng bản địa, "the number of birds is amazing, including several rare species" → wildlife (F). Bẫy: "hardly get a glimpse of the sea" nên không phải seashore.

15.why: Từ cổng lên hồ, đi nửa vòng bờ đông hồ rồi rẽ ra bờ biển; khu chim nằm nhìn ra một hòn đảo nhỏ.

16.why: Bãi tắm an toàn nhất: "follow the path north from the park entrance, but before you get to the lake, turn right… down to the beach".

17.why: Từ phía bắc cổng đi về Okiwi Bay, men bờ biển rồi rẽ phải sang Rocky Bay, qua cầu tàu (wharf) là tới con tàu cũ.

18.why: Đi vòng quanh hồ sang bờ bên kia, tiếp tục lên bắc; trước tháp nước (water tower) thì rẽ trái ra bờ biển.

19.why: "Take the first path on the left… around behind Okiwi Bay. The monument is out at the end there on the headland".

20.why: Ki-ốt nước "beside the lake, right on the water's edge".

21.why: Hai điểm bị chê: nhân viên quá đông ("too many of them… wasting money on wages") → B; và quảng cáo tới trường học chưa nhắm đúng ("advertising isn't targeted enough") → E. Hoạt động giáo dục thì được khen "great" nên D sai.

22.why: Hai điểm bị chê: nhân viên quá đông ("too many of them… wasting money on wages") → B; và quảng cáo tới trường học chưa nhắm đúng ("advertising isn't targeted enough") → E. Hoạt động giáo dục thì được khen "great" nên D sai.

23.why: Lo ngại 1: "Companies might think we know more than we actually do" → tạo kỳ vọng sai ở doanh nghiệp (C). Lo ngại 2: "we haven't devoted enough time to other parts of the course" → A. Còn thực tập thì "boosts your confidence" nên D sai.

24.why: Lo ngại 1: "Companies might think we know more than we actually do" → tạo kỳ vọng sai ở doanh nghiệp (C). Lo ngại 2: "we haven't devoted enough time to other parts of the course" → A. Còn thực tập thì "boosts your confidence" nên D sai.

25.why: Phần lịch sử: trọng tâm phải là hiện tại và tương lai, "Perhaps we should shorten this? – I think we should" → reduce the length (H).

26.why: Phần tổ chức quản lý sợ dài và chán; giảng viên gợi ý "a slide with a graphic showing the organisational structure" → include visual input (D).

27.why: Phần tài chính: định phỏng vấn giám đốc kế toán nhưng giảng viên bảo "keep this part to the minimum… we'll go with what we've got" → leave it as it is (B). Bẫy: F (interview) bị gạt đi.

28.why: Phần marketing: "get the audience to give a couple of suggestions… keeps them engaged" → involve the listeners directly (E).

29.why: Không thích cái tên "Key Problems", đổi thành "key challenges" → change the title (C).

30.why: Định nói về một điểm du lịch, giảng viên hỏi "Will that be enough?" → "Maybe two different attractions then?" → give an additional example (G).

31.why: Trước đây thực vật bị coi là sinh vật "essentially passive".

32.why: Great Lakes Sea Rocket là "a wild plant which grows on beaches".

33.why: "When the sea rocket detects other plants growing nearby it quickly grows additional roots" để tranh chất dinh dưỡng.

34.why: Sagebrush và thorn apple nhận biết cây bên cạnh "by sensing properties of the light that is reflected from them".

35.why: "Each plant species has what you could call its own signature".

36.why: Dodder "doesn't have the ability to make sugar by converting nutrients from the soil" nên phải ký sinh.

37.why: Dodder hại cây trồng như alfalfa "as well as potatoes and different varieties of citrus".

38.why: Dodder tìm vật chủ "by sensing the chemicals that other plants release into the soil and air".

39.why: Khi dò môi trường "it rotates in a circle" rồi mọc thẳng về phía vật chủ.

40.why: Các hiện tượng này giờ "quite easy to observe using up-to-date equipment" (up-to-date = modern).
